QuestInfo.name: [Spring Valley] Teaching Fear - Otters
QuestInfo.0: Navy Tail has a top secret calling to 'aid' the creatures of Spring Valley. \r\nJoin her, and teach survival instincts to the innocent, sheltered creatures of Spring Valley!
QuestInfo.1: The creatures of Spring Valley have lived in peace for so long that they've grown naive. Navy Tail wants to teach them the life skill of running away from hunters. They have to be cautious if they want to survive!
QuestInfo.2: You helped Navy Tail teach the animals to fear for their lives and distrust humans. Now they'll be fine if, er, when real hunters arrive.

0.0: Oh, dear. The silly creatures of Spring Valley are too trusting. They'll walk right up to you, even eat out of your hand! They've never known a harsh word in their life!
0.1: But someday, if they don't learn better, they'll be hunted down by vile hunters. I'm here to make sure that never happens.
0.2: I can't always be here to tell them not to take candy from strange hunters, you know? No, no, we have to teach them to survive on their own. \r\n#b#eWhat do you say? Want to help me teach the creatures to flee in fear when they so much as hear a loud noise?

yes.0: I'm glad we're on the same page. \r\nFirst, attack 200 #o9390985# and 50 #o9390986# monsters. The sacrifice of the few will enrich the survival instincts of the many.
yes.1: Remember, we're doing this to protect the wildlife, not to hurt them, even though you will, in fact, be hurting them... You've gotta think Big Picture.

no.0: You're not very forward-thinking, are you? Attacking them is for their own good. Or maybe you just don't care if hunters poach them to extinction...

1.0: You did it! I'm so relieved.

yes.0: Good, good. The creatures now flee when they hear so much as the flap of a butterfly wing.
yes.1: Don't be sad we can't approach the creatures anymore... This is MUCH better than finding out later that the animals were hurt by some heartless hunter!

mob.0: Not done yet? You have to strengthen your resolve! \r\nI know, it's tough to hurt them, but teaching them to live in fear and distrust is for their own good!
